content.thinking:
I need to flag a discrepancy: the admin change record shows the flag toggled on at a time that's actually after the observed onset in the logs, which conflicts with the narrative that the toggle caused the onset — I should note this without stating specific figures myself, instead referencing the documented timestamps.

On mitigation, the responder reverted the flag off and paged the checkout team, but the verification check happened essentially immediately after the revert, which seems too early to confirm the fix actually resolved the service — so the mitigation's effectiveness was never properly validated before being judged unsuccessful. For root cause, the enabled flag activated a code path that triggers a division by zero in the spend summary logic.

I should avoid citing specific figures and instead reference the named metrics provided, since using raw numbers isn't appropriate here.

For the file path, I'll stick with the filename itself rather than citing the specific line number, to stay safe on the no-figures rule. For duration and timing, I'll reference the named placeholders for detection delay and alert timing rather than hardcoding values.

Now since there are no existing action items, I need to start proposing some, numbered sequentially.

Drafting the action items: verify recovery against the wait window before closing (mitigate), fix the division-by-zero guard in spend_summary (prevent), roll out flags gradually with automated error checks (prevent), fix the change-feed query so flag toggles are captured and correlated with alerts since one query returned zero changes despite a flag change (detect/process), and flag that the incident was resolved by a human while verification was still pending (process). I also want to note the "got lucky" angle, since only a fraction of traffic was affected, which ties into contributing factors and lessons learned.

Now I'm building out the impact section — roughly a third of traffic failed that otherwise wouldn't have, specifically shoppers' account pages, peaking at some worst-case error rate. Then the causal chain: account page requests failed for about a third of users, each failure traced to a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, caused by the monthly-spend-feature flag being enabled, with logs showing it turned on around 15:18 and later turned off.

I'm ruling out other causes — no deploy or production change, unrelated ClientDisconnected errors that predate onset, and identical replica hardware across the board — while noting the actual division-by-zero logic itself isn't shown. I flag a timing inconsistency: the admin's flag toggle timestamp comes after the incident's onset, yet logs show the flag already active earlier, so treating these as the same event leaves an unexplained discrepancy I should record carefully. I also note the revert hasn't been shown to actually resolve the issue yet.

action_items.item: Fix the division by zero in the spend summary code (spend_summary.py) by guarding the zero divisor, and add a test that covers that input before the flag is enabled again.
Roll out flags like monthly-spend-feature to a small share of traffic first, with an automatic rollback if the error rate on the affected pages rises.
Include feature-flag toggles from the flag provider in the production change events the Investigator queries, so a flag change near the onset shows up as a change.

Make the post-action check wait for its stated window before judging a mitigation. Do not let the incident be closed while that verification is pending, and re-check the error rate after the flag revert to confirm recovery.
Add an alert or dashboard annotation that links a flag toggle to a jump in error rate on the same service, so it surfaces before the paging rule's wait ends.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate went from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while broken, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. That is {errors_rise} of traffic failing that otherwise would not have, and it was still the case when the incident was closed.
The failing requests each raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in the spend summary code, spend_summary.py. These errors appear from the onset at {began} through the end of the window read.

That code path ran because the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on. Before the onset the service logged the flag as off. From the onset it logged evaluations as on. The change feed shows the flag switched on by admin.

Other explanations were ruled out. The 24 hours of production change events showed no deploy or release on the service. The ClientDisconnected errors were shoppers closing connections, and they were logged before the onset. All three replicas ran on the same GPU type, so nothing pointed at placement. The record does not show why the spend summary code divides by zero, for example which accounts or inputs give a zero divisor. The chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or guard was seen on the spend summary path against a zero divisor. The flag was switched on in production without any gradual rollout or error-rate check being seen.

The change-event query read no production changes for the 24 hours before the onset, although the flag provider showed a recent flag change. Flag toggles were not visible in the change feed the Investigator read, which weakened the link from onset to cause.

Argus checked the service right after reverting the flag, before the window it had said it would wait for. It judged the action withdrawn without a fair read of the effect. A person closed the incident in the same moment, so the record does not show whether the revert fixed the errors.

The paging rule needs the condition to hold for {rule_waits} before it fires. Shoppers therefore hit errors for {alert_raised - began} before anyone was paged, and no flag-linked early signal was seen.

input.executive_summary: Shoppers on io-shop saw account pages fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, so {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have. The service was broken for at least {duration}, a lower bound, because it was not back to normal when the incident was closed. The cause was a feature flag, monthly-spend-feature, which turned on a code path that crashes with a division by zero. The alert fired at {alert_raised} after its {rule_waits} wait. Argus reverted the flag to off. Its check ran straight away and still saw the incident's error level, so it judged the action withdrawn. A person then closed the incident from PagerDuty, kept the flag off and paged the checkout team. The record does not show the service recovering.

got_lucky: Only a share of account page requests failed, not all of them. The failing path was behind a flag that could be switched off at once.
went_well: Argus formed the leading candidate from the logs within seconds and tied it to the flag. The ZeroDivisionError log line and the flag-on evaluations pointed at the same cause.
The mitigation was quick and low-risk: reverting a flag, which touches no deploy.
A person kept the flag off and paged the checkout team, who own the follow-up.
went_wrong: The revert was judged withdrawn from a check taken before its wait window began, so the record shows no confirmed recovery.
The incident was closed from PagerDuty while the service still looked broken at the incident's level.
The change feed read no changes although a flag change existed, and the flag change's timestamp is later than the onset.
